plain_claim: At a call site `IsCallSite p f b F ci G` (function `f` of `p` is `F`, its block `b` ends in the call `ci`, whose callee is `G`), suppose: every local mentioned by `F` and by `G` is below its declared count (`LocalsBounded F`, `LocalsBounded G`); every jump target of `F` is one of its blocks (`BlocksBounded F`); `F` and `G` satisfy `ScopesWF` (scope `0` exists and carries neither `inlined` nor `inlinedParent`, every `inlinedParent` link of scope `i` points to an index `t < i`, and every scope named by a `loc` statement or call is in range); callee locals `1 ≤ i < G.nlocals` go to host slots at or above `F.nlocals` (`SlotsFresh`) that are pairwise distinct (`SlotsInjective`); the return place goes to a temporary `t` (`cfg.ret = .temp t`) with `F.nlocals ≤ t` and `t` different from every callee slot (`TempFresh`); `continue` edges are redirected, `resume` is rewritten by the call's unwind action and the `rustc` scope-link rule is used; and `F.caps = G.caps` (equal lists). Then `BehEquiv p (inline p f b cfg)`: from every entry, every finite observation of `run` of either program is a prefix of an observation of the other, so the maximal event sequences (including cleanup `out` events, in order, and `loc` events) and the outcomes (including `ub`, `capFault`, `aborted` and `unwound`) coincide.

`F.caps = G.caps` is equality of lists (order and multiplicity matter), not equality as sets; `p.abi` is an arbitrary function of the list. Whether set-equal, order-distinct lists suffice is not examined (no counterexample for them is proved here).

One inlining step. `inline p f b cfg` replaces function `f` and leaves the callee `G` in `p.fns`, so this says nothing about removing `G`. `IsCallSite` allows direct self-recursion (`ci.callee = f`) and call sites inside cleanup blocks; no claim is made about termination of an inlining pass. The toy has no `catch` or search-phase unwinding, no double-panic rule beyond explicit `terminate` actions, no projections, borrows, storage markers, generics, recursion limits or debug information; values are unbounded naturals (`Rvalue.add` does not wrap); a missing call argument is read as `0` and extra arguments are ignored (`argOr`, `bindArgs`).
